## Executive Summary

Litware Terminal Services (LTS) operates at a critical inflection point: Q1-2026 revenue averaged $7.56M per month ($90.7M annualized), up 57% over FY2025 [1], while all four loaders and three stackers run at 100% utilization [2]. Director of Operations Owen Pratt manages this fleet scheduling daily in Excel, calling it his "central trading desk," where he manually matches equipment to projects under non-trivial constraints — only two of four loaders can perform "new build," and only two of three stackers can access the Central Reload Area pipeline [3]. This paper evaluates whether deploying a constraint-aware AI scheduling engine could unlock meaningful incremental throughput and EBITDA from this already-saturated fleet.

The core thesis is compelling but requires calibration. At LTS's Q1-2026 gross margin of 59.3% and largely fixed operating expenses (~$2.55M/month), incremental revenue from better scheduling carries an **incremental EBITDA margin of approximately 59%** [4]. However, the opportunity's original claim of 5–10% throughput improvement warrants scrutiny. Academic and industry evidence from adjacent industrial and construction sectors points to **2–6% gains from equipment-level scheduling optimization** [5] and up to 15–20% only when combined with broader process redesign [6]. Given that LTS's transition times between projects are already short (6–12 hours per Colin, Director of Operations) [7], we recommend modeling a **conservative 2–5% throughput band**, yielding **$1.1M–$2.72M in incremental annual EBITDA** against an estimated implementation investment of $170K–$340K.

The critical insight is that **operating expenses are largely fixed** at approximately $2.55M per month [4]. Subcontractor and hauler costs ($5.09M in Q1-2026) are the largest COGS component at 55.2% of total COGS and are volume-proportional. Consequently, incremental revenue from optimized scheduling flows through to EBITDA at the gross margin rate of approximately 59.3%, because the fixed operating cost base is already fully absorbed [4].

#### Payback Analysis

| Component | Low Estimate | High Estimate |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| Phase 1: Decision Rule Digitization | $35.3K | $85K |
| Phase 2: Optimization Engine + UI | $85K | $212K |
| Phase 3: Real-Time Integration | $63.8K | $128K |
| **Total Investment** | **$191K** | **$425K** |
| Annual Incremental EBITDA (2–5%) | $1.07M | $2.69M |
| **Payback Period** | **2–5 months** | **2–5 months** |

#### Important Caveats on the Revenue Baseline

It is important to note that the Q1-2026 annualized revenue of $90.7M significantly exceeds LTS's own 2026 budget of $78M [17], and the trailing twelve months (April 2025–March 2026) actual revenue was $67.6M with an EBITDA margin of only 17.8% [24]. The Q1-2026 period included unusually strong months (February at $7.99M and March at $9.26M), and LTS's revenue exhibits significant seasonality with a confirmed semi-annual cycle [18]. Using the 2026 budget of $78M as a more conservative revenue baseline, the 2–5% throughput band would yield **$0.935M–$2.3M in incremental annual EBITDA** — still an attractive return on a sub-$425K investment.

## Implementation Approach

### Technical Requirements

| Component | Technology | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| Optimization Solver | Google OR-Tools (CP-SAT) | Open-source, proven on constraint scheduling, no license cost |
| Data Layer | Python + SQLite/PostgreSQL | Structured storage for project, equipment, and schedule data |
| Visualization | Power BI or web-based Gantt | Familiar Microsoft ecosystem; visual what-if scenarios |
| Fleet Telemetry | Samsara (future Phase 3) | GPS, engine diagnostics, real-time position data |
| Integration | Python APIs + Claude AI | Extend Owen's existing Claude workflow for data extraction |
